                    na = c("", "NA", "#N/A")) |>
  # make column names lowercase snake_case

  distinct() |>

  mutate(
    type = factor(type, levels = c("h", "u", "t"),
                  labels = c("House", "Unit", "Townhouse")),
    method = factor(method,
                    levels = c("S", "SP", "PI", "VB", "SA"),
                    labels = c("Sold", "Sold prior", "Passed in",
                               "Vendor bid", "Sold after auction")),
    # combine the three small "Victoria" regions into one level
    region_group = if_else(str_detect(regionname, "Victoria"),
                           "Regional Victoria", regionname) |>
      factor()
  ) |>
  # keep the response and candidate predictors
  select(price, rooms, distance, bathroom, car,
         type, method, region_group)

title: Predicting Melbourne Housing Prices
text:
Metric
Since we chose price as the response, we will use root mean squared error (RMSE) as the metric to evaluate our regression models. Let us define the RMSE as:
\[
\text{RMSE} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(y_i - \hat{y}_i\right)^2}
\] where \(y_i\) is the actual sale price and \(\hat{y}_i\) is the model’s predicted price for the \(i\)th sale.

housing_metrics <- metric_set(rmse, mae)

title: Predicting Melbourne Housing Prices
text:
Regression Tree

What is a regression tree?


Firring a regression tree model

tree_spec <- decision_tree(cost_complexity = tune(), 
                           tree_depth = tune(), 
                           min_n = 20) |>
  set_engine("rpart") |>
  set_mode("regression")

tree_wkf <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(housing_recipe) |>
  add_model(tree_spec)


tree_grid <- expand_grid(cost_complexity = 10^seq(-5, -1, length.out = 5),
                         tree_depth = c(2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12))

tree_fits <- tree_wkf |>
  tune_grid(resamples = housing_folds,
            grid = tree_grid,
            metrics = housing_metrics)


tree_fits |>
  collect_metrics() |>
  filter(.metric == "rmse") |>
  arrange(mean)

title: Predicting Melbourne Housing Prices
text:
Random Forest

What is a random forest?


Fitting a random forest model

rf_spec <- rand_forest(mtry = tune(), trees = 500) |>
  set_engine("ranger",
             importance = "impurity",
             num.threads = parallel::detectCores()) |>
  set_mode("regression")

rf_wkf <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(housing_recipe) |>
  add_model(rf_spec)


rf_grid <- tibble(mtry = 1:7) # every possible number of predictors to consider at each split

rf_fits <- rf_wkf |>
  tune_grid(resamples = housing_folds,
            grid = rf_grid,
            metrics = housing_metrics)


rf_fits |>
  collect_metrics() |>
  filter(.metric == "rmse") |>
  arrange(mean)
